title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 80
paragraphs: Having heard this, he went his way. Pausanias then issued a proclamation that no one should lay hands on the spoils, and he ordered the Helots to gather the things together. They accordingly dispersed about the camp and found tents furnished with gold and silver, beds overlaid with gold and silver, mixing bowls of gold, and cups and other drinking vessels. They also found sacks laid on wagons, in which there turned out to be cauldrons of gold and silver; and from the dead bodies lying there they stripped bracelets, collars, and also their swords if they were of gold — for embroidered clothing was of no account. The Helots stole many of the things and sold them to the Aeginetans, but many also they delivered up — as many as they could not conceal. So the great wealth of the Aeginetans first came from this: they bought the gold from the Helots, pretending that it was bronze.
